text:
maya: quick RFC sketch — we need a compact OTEL span name + attribute keyset for LLM requests so dashboards and exporters can reliably compute cost/token and cache-hit metrics. sharing a draft, want feedback :eyes:

sam: +1 on doing this. can we make span names compact and stable? e.g. `llm.request` for the whole HTTP/gRPC request, `llm.infer` for the inner model call that has token counts. simpler to query.

leo: agree on compact names. also +1 to put version in attributes not the name. name should be the operation.

anika: some constraints: exporters (Datadog/OTLP) have different tag limits. keep attribute keys short but semantic. avoid huge JSON blobs. also we need to be careful with any prompt text — never put full prompt in an attribute. use hashes only.

maya: here's the draft keyset I sketched — short keys, hierarchical but short:```
span.name: llm.request or llm.infer
llm.model: gptx-13b
llm.model_ver: v2
llm.kind: chat|completion|embedding
llm.input_tok: 45
llm.output_tok: 512
llm.total_tok: 557
llm.cache_hit: 1 
llm.batched: 0
llm.prompt_hash: sha256:abcd...
llm.quant: q4_0
llm.hw: a100-80gb
llm.route: region-us-west1|dedicated
llm.trace_id: <OTEL trace id>
```
 Thoughts?

sam: love it. couple proposals: rename `llm.input_tok` -> `llm.tokens.request` and `llm.output_tok` -> `llm.tokens.generated` to make units explicit. also add `llm.batch_size` when batching is used.

leo: add `llm.kv_cache_hits` and `llm.kv_cache_lookups` if we want to compute hit ratio. kv cache details are useful for cost analysis.

anika: retention/exporter notes: for hosted telemetry we keep detailed token-level spans for 7d and aggregated metrics for 90d. for enterprise with longer retention we'll drop full token counts past 30d to avoid storage blowup. need a flag attr `llm.sensitive=false|true` (true -> strip prompt_hashing/limit retention) 

maya: good call. adding `llm.sensitive`. Also debating sampling: sample 100% for errors, 10% for success for high-volume embedding endpoints. We should expose `llm.sample_rate` attr so downstream exporters can reconstruct rates.

sam: about span boundaries: do we emit one span per HTTP request (covers routing + model call) and a child span for `llm.infer` that includes model-level attrs? that makes dashboards show routing overhead vs model latency.

maya: yes that's the plan. root span `llm.request` has routing attrs (`llm.route`, `llm.client_tier`, `quota_group`) and child `llm.infer` has `llm.model*` and token counts + `llm.cache_*`.

leo: example query for cache hit ratio on the dashboard: `sum(llm_kv_cache_hits) / sum(llm_kv_cache_lookups)` over a period. make sure we export those as numeric metrics too (OTLP gauge) to avoid expensive span scans.

anika: exporters: OTLP proto will carry attributes as keys. Datadog needs mapping -> tag. we need a short approved list in our telemetry config to prevent free-form keys. propose whitelist: `llm.model, llm.model_ver, llm.kind, llm.tokens.request, llm.tokens.generated, llm.kv_cache_hits, llm.kv_cache_lookups, llm.cache_hit, llm.batched, llm.batch_size, llm.quant, llm.route, llm.sensitive, llm.sample_rate`

maya: +1. also UX for rollouts: include `llm.rollout_id` and `llm.variant` attributes so we can A/B by model variant in console charts.

sam: one more: `llm.cost_estimate_cents` as optional attr computed by routing layer so cost dashboards can show per-request estimated charge. keep as integer cents.

anika: privacy note again: ensure `llm.prompt_hash` is a one-way hash, no reversible content. mark `llm.sensitive=true` if the request contained user PII or customer opted out of retention. That will trigger retention rules in pipeline.

maya: I'll draft a telemetry RFC doc and a small mapping table for exporters. will add the whitelist + example queries. tagging infra to review rate-limiting of trace ingestion. infra-bot can you open a ticket for ingestion quota review? :slightly_smiling_face: 

infra-bot: created issue INF-2029 "trace-ingest: LLM telemetry volume and exporter whitelist" assigned to @infra. link: https://redwood/issue/INF-2029

leo: ok next steps: maya to create RFC, anika to draft retention rules, sam to add console chart wireframes for cost/token and cache-hit ratio. I'll stub OTLP->Datadog mapping.

maya: thanks all. I'll post RFC link later. :rocket:
